title: What is the balance when a purchase costs more than the account?
description: A bank account holds one hundred and thirty rupees, and a business purchase of one hundred and fifty rupees is paid from it. The debit is bigger than the balance, so the balance becomes a negative number. Keeko doubts that a balance can go below zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a debit is bigger than the balance, the balance goes below zero and shows money owed. Watch for students who say a balance can never be negative.

source: The next day you make a major purchase for your business of ₹150 (again a debit). What is your bank balance now? ______ Is this possible?
video_script.why: The child takes a debit bigger than the balance and sees that the balance can become negative.
video_script.substitution: Take the debit away from the balance; the part of the debit the balance cannot cover shows as a negative balance.
video_script.wrong_move: says a balance can never go below zero, so the answer is zero, instead of letting the unpaid part of the debit show as a negative number
video_script.payoff_line: The balance is negative twenty rupees.
maths_rules: a debit of ₹150 is money going out: −150
the unpaid ₹20 shows as a negative balance
some banks allow a negative balance for a short time and may charge a fee or interest
video_script.design: One idea: a debit bigger than the balance leaves a negative balance. The money bar empties and the last twenty rupees of the debit push the balance below the empty line. Keeko thinks a balance cannot go below zero.
